title: Victoria Falls
text: Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the Zambezi River on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe in southern Africa. It is considered one of the world's largest waterfalls based on its combined width of 1,708 meters and height of 108 meters. The local Kololo tribe name for the falls is 'Mosi-oa-Tunya,' meaning 'the smoke that thunders,' referring to the spray and noise generated. Scottish explorer David Livingstone was the first European to view the falls, in 1855, and named them after Queen Victoria. Victoria Falls is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major tourist attraction. The Zambezi River above the falls averages an annual flow of approximately 1,088 cubic meters per second.
